title: Algebraic Differentials Separability and Smooth Local Presentations

items.title: Ag universal algebraic differentials
items.statement: For a map of commutative rings A→B, Ω_{B/A} is the B-module on symbols db, b∈B, modulo d(b+b′)=db+db′, d(bb′)=b db′+b′ db, and d(a)=0 for a∈A. An A-derivation into a B-module is additive, A-constant, and satisfies Leibniz.
items.strategy: Construct the quotient of a free B-module; verify the displayed relations make d an A-derivation. No finite presentation is assumed.

items.title: Ag differentials universal property
items.statement: For every B-module M, composition with d gives a natural B-module isomorphism Hom_B(Ω_{B/A},M)≅Der_A(B,M).
items.strategy: A derivation assigns an image to every free symbol and kills exactly the additivity, Leibniz, and A-constant relators. Conversely any map from the quotient is a derivation; verify naturality in M.

items.title: Ag polynomial quotient differentials
items.statement: For P=A[x_1,…,x_n] and B=P/I, Ω_{P/A} is free on dx_i and I/I²→B⊗_PΩ_{P/A}→Ω_{B/A}→0 is exact, with f mod I²↦df. If I=(f_1,…,f_c), Ω_{B/A} is the cokernel of the Jacobian matrix (∂f_j/∂x_i). The left map need not be injective.
items.strategy: Use coordinate derivations to prove independence of dx_i and Leibniz to generate. Check d(I²)⊂IΩ; by the universal property, derivations of B are precisely derivations of P that kill I. The f_j generate I/I², hence every df is their B-linear combination.

items.title: Ag differentials localization base change
items.statement: For A→B and multiplicative U⊂B, V⊂A whose image lies in U, Ω_{U^{-1}B/V^{-1}A}≅U^{-1}Ω_{B/A}. For A→A′ and B′=B⊗_A A′, Ω_{B′/A′}≅B′⊗_BΩ_{B/A}. An arbitrary A-algebra map B→C induces C⊗_BΩ_{B/A}→Ω_{C/A}, without an isomorphism claim.
items.strategy: For localization derive d(b/u)=u^{-1}db-bu^{-2}du and use the universal property in both directions. For base change, an A′-derivation of B⊗_A A′ is uniquely its restriction to B extended by zero on A′; apply Yoneda. State separately the general map.

items.title: Ag differentials transitivity
items.statement: For A→B→C there is a natural exact sequence C⊗_BΩ_{B/A}→Ω_{C/A}→Ω_{C/B}→0. The first arrow is not asserted injective.
items.strategy: The second map is the quotient imposing db=0 for b∈B; its kernel is exactly the C-span of these db, which is the image of the first map. Give k→k[x]→k by x↦0 as a noninjective left example: k⊗Ω_{k[x]/k}≅k dx maps to Ω_{k/k}=0.

items.title: Ag separating transcendence basis
items.statement: For a finitely generated field extension K/k, a separating transcendence basis t_1,…,t_r is a transcendence basis such that K/k(t_1,…,t_r) is finite separable. The empty basis is allowed when K/k is finite separable.
items.strategy: Use finite generation to make the algebraic remainder finite; distinguish this from every algebraic extension of a perfect base being separable, since k(t_i) need not be perfect.

items.title: Ag separating transcendence basis perfect field
items.statement: Every finitely generated extension K/k of a perfect field has a separating transcendence basis. In characteristic p, the proof uses p-power linear independence and finite-generator exchanges; it does not infer that k(t_1,…,t_r) is perfect.
items.strategy: Choose a finite transcendence basis t for K/k and write K=k(t,α_1,…,α_s). For perfect k, pth powers of k-linearly independent elements remain k-linearly independent. At each induction stage, a finite separable extension over the current rational-function field has a primitive generator β; adjoining the next α_j leaves at most one inseparable generator, so the published primitive-element theorem writes the enlarged finite extension as k(u,γ). Choose an irreducible minimal-total-degree relation F(u,γ). If every partial derivative vanished, the p-power independence would give a relation of smaller total degree; hence some partial derivative is nonzero. Exchange γ for the variable corresponding to that derivative. Gauss irreducibility gives a separable algebraic extension over the exchanged transcendence basis. Repeat through the finite generator list. Characteristic zero is immediate.

items.title: Ag field differentials separable rank
items.statement: If K/k is finitely generated and separably generated by t_1,…,t_r, then dt_1,…,dt_r form a K-basis of Ω_{K/k}. For any characteristic-zero tower k⊂K⊂L, assuming AC to choose a transcendence basis when needed, L⊗_KΩ_{K/k}→Ω_{L/k} is injective.
items.strategy: Localize the polynomial differential basis to k(t); the transitivity cokernel is Ω_{K/k(t)}=0 by differentiating separable minimal polynomials. To prove independence, extend each coordinate derivation across the finite separable extension using D(α)=−D(P)(α)/P′(α). For the characteristic-zero tower, choose a transcendence basis of L/K using AC, extend arbitrary k-derivations K→L by zero on it, then uniquely across the remaining separable algebraic extension; dual evaluations separate elements of L⊗Ω_{K/k}. Explicitly identify this choice use.

items.title: Ag separable residue cotangent sequence
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian local k-algebra with maximal ideal m and finitely generated separable residue field κ/k. Then 0→m/m²→Ω_{R/k}⊗_Rκ→Ω_{κ/k}→0 is exact. At a closed point of a finite-type k-algebra with finite separable residue field, Ω_{κ/k}=0, so the first arrow is an isomorphism.
items.strategy: Apply the conormal sequence to R→κ for right exactness. Replace R by R/m² using the quotient differential formula. Lift a separating transcendence basis to R/m²; denominators stay units. Lift a primitive separable generator and correct it by δ∈m/m² using P(y+δ)=P(y)+P′(y)δ to split κ→R/m². The split quotient derivation into m/m² is a left inverse to d, proving injectivity. For finite separable κ/k, differentiate its minimal polynomial to obtain Ωκ/k=0.

items.title: Ag field extension of schemes
items.statement: Assume AC. For any k-scheme X and field extension K/k, glue Spec(A_i⊗_kK) over an affine cover X=∪Spec A_i to form X_K. The construction is independent of cover, X_K→X has affine fibres Spec(κ(x)⊗_kK), and (X_K)_L≅X_L canonically for K⊂L.
items.strategy: Use localization-tensor compatibility on principal affine intersections; refine arbitrary overlaps by principal affine opens, then apply affine-scheme gluing and uniqueness. The fibre at x is the affine tensor product with κ(x); associativity of tensor gives repeated base change, respecting all overlap maps. AC is inherited from the published affine-scheme and gluing constructions, via existence of maximal ideals.

references.title: Stacks Algebra 10.131.12 and standard affine tensor base change

items.title: Ag geometrically regular algebra and fibre
items.statement: A finite-type k-algebra A is geometrically regular over k if A⊗_kK is a regular Noetherian ring for every finitely generated field extension K/k; the later field-test lemma proves regularity after arbitrary field extensions. For a finitely presented R-algebra S and q∈Spec S over p∈Spec R, the fibre is geometrically regular at q if for every field extension K/κ(p), every local ring at a prime of (S⊗_Rκ(p))⊗_κ(p)K lying over q is regular. A fibre is geometrically regular if it is so at every point. Empty fibres satisfy the local condition vacuously.
items.strategy: Define global geometric regularity by regularity at every prime of each finite-generated scalar extension. Define the pointwise fibre condition using every extension and every point over q so that a rational point over an algebraic closure of κ(q) is covered without a later theorem. The field-test lemma will equate the global finite-extension condition with the all-extension pointwise condition. Keep geometric regularity distinct from ordinary regularity and from smoothness, whose equivalence is proved later.

items.title: Ag standard smooth algebra
items.statement: A standard smooth R-presentation is S=(R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c))_g, 0≤c≤n, in which a c×c Jacobian minor is invertible in S; c=0 gives a polynomial localization. A finite-presentation map is locally standard smooth at q if an affine localization around q has such a presentation.
items.strategy: Record equation/variable convention and that an invertible minor may be moved to the first c variables. A further principal localization can be encoded by adjoining z with zg−1=0, preserving a block invertible minor.

items.title: Ag base change of standard smooth presentations
items.statement: For a ring map R→R′ and a standard smooth presentation S≅(R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c))_g with invertible leading c×c Jacobian minor h, the base change S′=R′⊗_R S is described by the same presentation over R′, with the image of h a unit; the isomorphism is unique and the relative dimension stays n−c.
items.strategy: Compare both algebras by universal properties: build Φ and τ from the quotient and localisation universal properties, show they are mutually inverse on generators, and note the image of h is again a unit and that the presentation is standard smooth over R′.

items.title: Ag standard smooth fibre regular parameters
items.statement: Assume AC. Let q⊆k[x_1,…,x_n] be prime over a field k with A=k[x]_q, and let f_1,…,f_c∈q have leading c×c Jacobian minor h∉q. Then the classes of the f_j in m/m² are κ-linearly independent, A is regular local, (f_1,…,f_c) is a regular sequence, and A/(f_1,…,f_c) is regular local of dimension dim A−c.
items.strategy: Use the conormal sequence to show the classes of the f_j are independent in m/m², extend them to a regular system of parameters of A, and read the quotient as a regular local ring of dimension dim A−c.

items.title: Ag local flatness regular parameters
items.statement: Assume AC. For a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings (R,m)→(S,n) and a finite S-module M, Tor_1^R(R/m,M)=0 implies that M is R-flat; M need not be finite over R. If R and S are regular local and images of a regular parameter system of R extend to a regular parameter system of S, then S is R-flat.
items.strategy: Use the Tor long exact sequence to propagate vanishing from R/m to all finite-length R-modules. For any ideal I⊂R compare I, m^n, I+m^n, and I∩m^n; finite-colength injections imply ker(I⊗M→M) comes from (I∩m^n)⊗M. Artin–Rees puts it in m^{n−c}(I⊗M); I⊗M is finite over S, and mS⊂n, so Krull intersection over S kills the kernel. For the parameter application, the Koszul resolution of R/m tensors to the acyclic Koszul complex on the images in S, giving Tor_1=0. AC is used through the published Krull-intersection Jacobson criterion and regular-parameter suppliers; it also covers the supplied DC Tor sequence.

items.title: Ag standard smooth flatness
items.statement: Assume AC. Every standard smooth R-algebra is finitely presented and flat over R, for an arbitrary commutative base ring R.
items.strategy: The presentation and localization are finitely presented (encode g^{-1} by zg−1). Descend the finitely many coefficients and the inverse-minor identity to a finitely generated Z-subalgebra R_0⊂R. This R_0 is Noetherian. At each prime of the descended algebra localize R_0 and the polynomial algebra. The minor gives linearly independent fibre differentials df_i, hence the f_i extend to regular parameters in the regular local polynomial fibre. Induct on i: the current quotient is R_0-flat, the next f_i is a fibre nonzerodivisor; Krull intersection in the Noetherian local polynomial quotient lifts injectivity, so the Tor sequence gives Tor_1^{R_0}(κ,further quotient)=0; apply the finite-S-module local-flatness lemma (the quotient is finite over itself). Local flatness patches; tensoring R_0→R preserves flatness. AC is inherited from the local-flatness and regular-ring suppliers.

items.title: Ag standard smooth regular geometric fibres
items.statement: Assume AC. For S=(R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c))_g standard smooth, every nonempty fibre over p∈Spec R stays regular after every extension of κ(p), and its irreducible components have dimension n−c. At a fibre prime q with ambient polynomial prime q′, the local fibre dimension is ht(q′)−c; it is not universally n−c.
items.strategy: Base change keeps the same invertible minor. In the regular local ambient polynomial ring over any field extension, the df_i are linearly independent in Ω⊗κ(q′); a linear relation among their classes in q′/q′² would differentiate to a relation among df_i, so the f_i extend to regular parameters. Repeated parameter quotient gives regular fibre local ring and dimension ht(q′)−c. Its component dimension is n−c by the affine finite-type dimension theorem and height c; localization only discards components. AC enters via the published regular-local parameter/dimension suppliers.

items.title: Ag flat local regularity ascent descent
items.statement: Assume AC. For a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings (R,m)→(S,n), if R and S/mS are regular then S is regular; if S is regular then R is regular. The second assertion is faithful local descent, without assuming the closed fibre regular.
items.strategy: For ascent, a regular parameter sequence of R stays S-regular by flatness; quotient successively and lift regularity from the regular closed fibre using the published regular-element lifting theorem. For descent let d=dim S and construct a possibly infinite R-free resolution of κ(m), with finite-rank terms at every stage because R is Noetherian. Tensor with the flat R-algebra S. Since regular S has global dimension d, the dth syzygy tensored with S is projective. Faithful flatness of the local map descends flatness of the original finite syzygy; finite-flat Noetherian makes it projective. Hence pd_R κ(m)≤d and Auslander–Buchsbaum–Serre makes R regular. AC is used to choose the resolution and inherited from the published regularity/global-dimension theorem. If d=0, S is a field and faithful flatness forces m=0, so R is a field without invoking the nth-syzygy statement (which assumes n≥1).

items.title: Ag finite field extension separable factorization
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finitely generated field extension K/k in characteristic p, there are finite purely inseparable extensions k′/k and K′/K such that K′/k′ is separably generated. No perfectness of k is assumed.
items.strategy: Choose a finite transcendence basis t and the separable core K_s of K/k(t), with K/K_s purely inseparable. Induct on [K:K_s]_i. If nontrivial, take β∉K_s with β^p=α∈K_s. For the separable minimal polynomial P of α over k(t), adjoining t_i^{1/p} and pth roots of the finitely many k-coefficients in its rational-function coefficients makes P a pth power coefficientwise. Its distinct roots then acquire pth roots inside the separable compositum, so β enters its new separable core; the inseparable degree falls. Iterate finitely many times. Keep k′ and K′ finite at every step. AC is inherited from the published separable-core and inseparable-degree suppliers, whose algebraic-closure construction uses Zorn.

items.title: Ag geometric regularity field tests
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite-type k-algebra A, geometric regularity is equivalent to regularity of A⊗_k k′ for every finite purely inseparable extension k′/k. It then persists for arbitrary field extensions; regularity descends through a faithfully flat scalar extension.
items.strategy: The forward direction is immediate. For a finitely generated K/k use the preceding inseparable/separable factorization K→K′ over k′. By hypothesis A_{k′} is regular. Present separably generated K′/k′ as the fraction field of a standard smooth localization of a finite polynomial quotient with separable derivative; standard-smooth flatness and regular-local ascent make A_{K′} regular. Flat-local regularity descent along K→K′ gives A_K regular. For arbitrary K, write K as filtered union of finitely generated subfields, descend any finite module over A_K to a finite presentation at a stage, use the uniform bound dim A_{K_i}≤dim A and the published regular-ring/global-dimension criterion, then flat base change. For faithful-flat descent of geometric regularity along k→K, given a test field E/k choose a prime of E⊗_kK and its residue field L, which receives E and K. Regularity of A_L follows from geometric regularity over K, and the faithfully flat local extension A_E→A_L descends regularity to A_E. The ring-regularity descent is the flat-local regularity lemma. Treat A=0 separately. For nonzero A, the uniform dimension bound follows from Noether normalization A finite over k[z_1,…,z_d]: after scalar extension, K[z_1,…,z_d] still injects and A_K is finite over it, so integral extensions preserve dimension d. This is independent of the chosen intermediate subfield.

items.title: Ag geometric regularity perfect base
items.statement: Assume AC. If k is perfect and A is a regular finite-type k-algebra, then A⊗_kK is regular for every field extension K/k.
items.strategy: A perfect k has no nontrivial finite purely inseparable extension. Apply the finite-extension test in the preceding lemma, including its arbitrary-extension passage. AC is inherited from that lemma; no assumption that K itself is perfect is made.

items.title: Ag perfect field jacobian regularity
items.statement: Assume AC. Let A=k[x_1,…,x_n]/I be finite type over a perfect field k. At a closed point x with maximal m and finite separable residue κ, A_m is regular iff the Jacobian of any generating set of I has rank n−dim A_m over κ. The regular locus is open; on every reduced irreducible component it contains a dense open. Local standard smooth charts extend the criterion to all scheme points.
items.strategy: At the closed point the ambient polynomial local ring has dimension n and the separable-residue cotangent sequence identifies m/m² with Ω_A/k⊗κ. The polynomial-quotient presentation gives dim cotangent=n−rank J, so regularity is exactly rank n−dim A_m, independent of generators. At any regular prime, its residue extension is separably generated over perfect k; the split cotangent sequence and the regular-quotient ideal theorem give local generators of I with a nonzero Jacobian minor. Nakayama kills the remaining relations nearby, so these minors define standard open charts directly, with no appeal to the later local-presentation theorem. For reduced components, the generic local ring is a field, hence regular; openness yields density. AC enters via geometric regularity and regular-local suppliers.

items.title: Ag geometrically regular fibres local presentation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let R→S be finitely presented and q∈Spec S over p∈Spec R. If S_q is R_p-flat and the fibre is geometrically regular at q, then after localizing S near q the map has a standard smooth presentation. This is the converse needed for smooth local charts.
items.strategy: Write S=R[x]/I near q with I finitely generated. Under AC, the polynomial ring over the fibre field κ(p) and its prime localization are regular, while geometric regularity makes the fibre quotient regular. The regular-quotient ideal theorem and Nakayama select c of the original generators that generate the fibre ideal locally. At a K-rational point over κ(q) in an algebraic closure K, the closed-point Jacobian criterion gives a nonzero c-minor; nonvanishing descends to q. Flatness of S_q over R_p and the Tor exact sequence make the kernel J of the selected-equation quotient have zero κ(p)-fibre. Nakayama kills J at q; localize further to kill the remaining relations and invert the minor. The resulting chart is standard smooth.

items.title: Ag standard smooth geometric regularity
items.statement: Assume AC. A finitely presented ring map R→S is locally standard smooth at every point iff it is flat and every fibre is geometrically regular. At an individual q the analogous equivalence uses flatness at q and geometric regularity at its fibre point. Over a field, finite-type geometric regularity is equivalent to local standard smoothness.
items.strategy: Forward: standard charts are finitely presented and flat and stay regular after all field changes. Reverse: apply the preceding local-presentation lemma at each q, then cover Spec S. Over a field flatness is automatic; use the field-test lemma to pass from finitely generated scalar extensions in the global definition to every extension in the pointwise definition, then apply the local-presentation lemma. AC is inherited through the two local lemmas.

items.title: Ag standard smooth base change composition
items.statement: Standard smooth presentations and locally standard smooth maps are stable under arbitrary ring base change and under composition; the relative dimensions of the displayed presentations add under composition. No assertion about fibre dimensions is made here.
items.strategy: Tensor the polynomial quotient and localization with the new base, preserving the invertible Jacobian minor. For composition, clear denominators in the second equations and its localization element, then order variables and equations so the combined Jacobian minor is block triangular with the two invertible minors on its diagonal. At a point, localize the second chart at the first chart’s witness as well. Relative dimension is (n−c)+(m−d); no regularity theorem or AC is used.

items.title: Ag submersion criterion standard smooth
items.statement: Assume AC. Let f:X→Y be a finite-type morphism between k-schemes that are locally standard smooth over k at k-rational points x and y=f(x). Then f is locally standard smooth at x iff f*:m_y/m_y²→m_x/m_x² is injective. If dim_xX=m and dim_yY=n, the fibre at x is regular of dimension m−n and the map is flat near x.
items.strategy: A local standard presentation yields a split injection of cotangent spaces via the block Jacobian. Conversely choose regular parameters y_1,…,y_n in O_{Y,y}; cotangent injectivity says their pulled-back classes are independent in m_x/m_x² and extend to regular parameters in O_{X,x}. Their Koszul complex resolves κ(y) after tensor to O_{X,x}, so the finite-S-module local criterion gives flatness. The fibre quotient by this regular sequence is regular of dimension m−n. At the k-rational point, present the fibre by polynomials over k; the separable-residue cotangent sequence (κ(x)=k), polynomial differential formula, and regular-quotient ideal theorem select local equations with a nonzero Jacobian minor, even when k is imperfect. Nakayama removes the other relations. Thus the fibre has a standard smooth chart and is geometrically regular there by the standard-smooth fibre lemma. Apply the preceding flat-plus-fibre local-presentation theorem to f. AC is used in the local-flatness and regular-parameter suppliers.

title: Algebraic Differentials Separability and Smooth Local Presentations — Examples

items.title: Ag differentials polynomial and hypersurface
items.statement: For A=k[x,y]/(y²−x³), Ω_{A/k}=(A dx⊕A dy)/(2y dy−3x² dx). At the origin the fibre of Ω has dimension two even when the curve has dimension one.
items.strategy: Apply the quotient formula; both coefficients vanish at (x,y), so the relation vanishes after tensoring with k. The calculation works in every characteristic, with coefficients 2 or 3 interpreted in k.

items.title: Ag differentials arbitrary map is not base change
items.statement: For k[x]→k by x↦0, k⊗_{k[x]}Ω_{k[x]/k}≅k·dx is nonzero while Ω_{k/k}=0; the natural map for an arbitrary algebra map is therefore not always an isomorphism.
items.strategy: Compute the polynomial module and the zero target module directly; identify the map as sending dx to d0=0. The square is not a tensor base-change square.

references.title: Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, relevant numbered lemmas

items.title: Ag separable and inseparable field differentials
items.statement: If E/k is finite separable, Ω_{E/k}=0. In characteristic p, for a∈k\k^p and L=k[t]/(t^p−a), Ω_{L/k}≅L·dt, even though L is a field.
items.strategy: For E use the published primitive-element theorem, differentiate its separable minimal polynomial P, and divide by P′(α), giving Ω_{E/k}=0. For L choose an irreducible factor Q of X^p−a and put α=X mod Q in the finite field k[X]/(Q). In that field X^p−a=(X−α)^p, so Q has only the root α. If deg Q>1 and Q′≠0, the derivative criterion would make Q separable, contradicting this repeated root; hence Q′=0 and deg Q=p. Degree one would give α∈k and a∈k^p. Thus X^p−a is irreducible and L is a field. The quotient differential formula gives d(t^p−a)=0 and Ω_{L/k}=L·dt.

items.title: Ag standard smooth hypersurface chart
items.statement: Over a field k of characteristic different from two, the hypersurface y²−x³=0 is standard smooth on D(y), because ∂(y²−x³)/∂y=2y is invertible there.
items.strategy: Localize the quotient at y, choose y as the first variable and the single equation, and display the 1×1 minor 2y, which is a unit. The remaining coordinate is free in the differential presentation.

items.title: Ag field change inseparable thickening
items.statement: If char k=p and a∉k^p, put L=k[t]/(t^p−a) with α=t mod (t^p−a). Then L⊗_kL≅L[u]/(u^p) via u=t⊗1−α; the base change is nonreduced.
items.strategy: To see L is a field, choose an irreducible factor Q of X^p−a; in k[X]/(Q) all roots of X^p−a coincide, so Q has one distinct root. A nonzero Q′ would make Q separable and force deg Q=1, contradicting a∉k^p. Therefore Q′=0 and deg Q=p, so X^p−a is irreducible. Tensor its defining quotient with L and translate t by α: t^p−a=(t−α)^p. The class u is nonzero (the quotient has basis 1,u,…,u^{p−1} over L) and nilpotent of order p.

references.title: Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, relevant numbered lemmas

items.title: Ag regular factors product not regular
items.statement: For a nontrivial finite purely inseparable L/k, the ring L is regular but L⊗_kL is not reduced and hence not regular; regularity of two field factors does not survive this tensor product.
items.strategy: For a degree-p subextension k(α)/k compute k(α)⊗_kk(α)=k(α)[u]/(u^p). For any nontrivial finite purely inseparable L/k choose α∈L\k with α^p∈k after a suitable p-power stage. The diagonal element α⊗1−1⊗α is nonzero by a k-linear basis argument and nilpotent. The multiplication kernel of L⊗_kL→L is generated by finitely many such diagonal differences and is nilpotent, so L⊗_kL is a zero-dimensional local ring with a nonzero nilpotent. A zero-dimensional regular local ring is a field by the definition of regularity, a contradiction.

items.title: Ag projection submersion parameters
items.statement: For π:A_k^{m+n}→A_k^m projecting to the first m coordinates at any k-rational point, pulled-back target parameters are independent, π is standard smooth with c=0, and every fibre is A_k^n of dimension n.
items.strategy: Write k[y_1,…,y_m,x_1,…,x_n] as a polynomial algebra over k[y_1,…,y_m]. Its c=0 chart is standard smooth directly. At a k-rational point the classes of y_i−a_i are part of the coordinate cotangent basis, so pullback is injective; quotient by them gives k[x_1,…,x_n] of dimension n. This explicit calculation uses no AC.
